shortDescription: NetApp ONTAP Run any REST API on ONTAP

options.name: accept_header
options.description: Value for the Accept request HTTP header. This is very infrequently needed, but required to read a file (see examples). For most cases, omit this field.  Set it to "multipart/form-data" when expecting such a format. By default the module is using "application/json" or "application/hal+json" when hal_linking is true.

options.name: api
options.description: The REST API to call (eg I(cluster/software), I(svms/svm)).

options.name: body
options.description: A dictionary for the info parameter

options.name: cert_filepath
options.description: path to SSL client cert file (.pem). not supported with python 2.6.

options.name: feature_flags
options.description: Enable or disable a new feature. This can be used to enable an experimental feature or disable a new feature that breaks backward compatibility. Supported keys and values are subject to change without notice.  Unknown keys are ignored.

options.name: files
options.description: A dictionary for the parameters when using multipart/form-data. This is very infrequently needed, but required to write a file (see examples) When present, requests will automatically set the Content-Type header to multipart/form-data.

options.name: force_ontap_version
options.description: Override the cluster ONTAP version when using REST. The behavior is undefined if the version does not match the target cluster. This is provided as a work-around when the cluster version cannot be read because of permission issues. See https://github.com/ansible-collections/netapp.ontap/wiki/Known-issues. This should be in the form 9.10 or 9.10.1 with each element being an integer number.

options.name: hal_linking
options.description: if true, HAL-encoded links are returned in the response.

options.name: hostname
options.description: The hostname or IP address of the ONTAP instance.

options.name: http_port
options.description: Override the default port (80 or 443) with this port

options.name: https
options.description: Enable and disable https. Ignored when using REST as only https is supported. Ignored when using SSL certificate authentication as it requires SSL.

options.name: key_filepath
options.description: path to SSL client key file.

options.name: lambda_config
options.description: Configuration parameters for AWS Lambda proxy functionality. These option and suboptions are only supported with REST.

options.name: method
options.description: The REST method to use.

options.name: password
options.description: Password for the specified user.

options.name: query
options.description: A list of dictionaries for the query parameters

options.name: use_lambda
options.description: Specifies if AWS Lambda proxy functionality should be used to connect to the ONTAP system. Supported only with REST.

options.name: use_rest
options.description: This module only supports REST. always -- will always use the REST API. A warning is issued if the module does not support REST.

options.name: username
options.description: This can be a Cluster-scoped or SVM-scoped account, depending on whether a Cluster-level or SVM-level API is required. For more information, please read the documentation U(https://docs.netapp.com/us-en/ontap/authentication/create-svm-user-accounts-task.html). Two authentication methods are supported 1. Basic authentication, using username and password. 2. SSL certificate authentication, using a ssl client cert file, and optionally a private key file. To use a certificate, the certificate must h

options.name: validate_certs
options.description: If set to C(no), the SSL certificates will not be validated. This should only set to C(False) used on personally controlled sites using self-signed certificates.

options.name: vserver_name
options.description: if provided, forces vserver tunneling.  username identifies a cluster admin account.

options.name: vserver_uuid
options.description: if provided, forces vserver tunneling.  username identifies a cluster admin account.

options.name: wait_for_completion
options.description: when true, POST/PATCH/DELETE can be handled synchronously and asynchronously. if the response indicates that a job is in progress, the job status is checked periodically until is completes. when false, the call returns immediately.
